Can You Study in China in English Without HSK?
How to separate teaching language, admission evidence, CSCA subjects, and graduation rules

English-taught programs may not use HSK as their admission-language test, but that does not create a universal HSK exemption. Check the exact program, its accepted English evidence, any CSCA subjects, and any Chinese-language requirement that applies later.
The short answer

Sometimes, for a specific English-taught program. There is no safe country-wide yes or no. Universities publish requirements at program level, and the language used in class is only one part of the decision. An English-taught route may ask for IELTS, TOEFL, another recognized test, or evidence of prior English-medium study. It may also publish separate academic or CSCA requirements.
Check four different rules

Keep these questions separate: What language is used for teaching? What language evidence is accepted for admission? Which CSCA examination language and subjects apply? Is Chinese proficiency required during study or before graduation? Treating these as one question is a common source of avoidable application errors.
What official examples show

Zhejiang University's 2026 undergraduate notice separates Chinese-taught and English-taught language evidence, and its English-program catalog publishes program-specific English thresholds and CSCA subjects. UIBE's published English undergraduate materials also list accepted English evidence. These examples prove that applicants must read the exact route; they do not create a rule for every university.
Build an evidence checklist before applying

Record the official program URL, teaching language, accepted English tests, minimum component scores if stated, exemption wording, CSCA subjects, application deadline, and the date you checked the notice. Save the source page or PDF with your application notes because universities can revise requirements between admission cycles.
How to make the final decision

Apply without HSK only when the current official program notice supports that conclusion and you meet every alternative language and academic condition. If the notice is incomplete or two official pages conflict, ask the university in writing and keep the response with your application record.
How to Shortlist Chinese Universities for an English-Taught Bachelor's Degree
A repeatable process based on verified program-level evidence

Start with eligible programs, then compare academic fit, language evidence, total cost, deadlines, and source quality. A shorter verified list is more useful than a long list built from outdated summaries.
Filter for eligibility before ranking

Begin with the current official program catalog and admissions notice. Confirm that the route is open to international applicants, taught in English, available for the intended intake, and compatible with your previous subjects and qualifications. Remove a program from the working list if any mandatory condition is not met.
Use one comparison table

Create columns for program, university, city, duration, tuition, other compulsory costs, accepted language evidence, CSCA subjects, academic prerequisites, deadline, scholarship options, application channel, and official-source date. Keep unknown fields visibly unknown instead of guessing.
Compare at program level

Requirements can differ inside the same university. Zhejiang University's 2026 English undergraduate catalog, for example, publishes different program details in the same official document. UIBE likewise maintains English-program information alongside a route-specific admissions page. University reputation alone cannot answer whether a particular route fits you.
Build a balanced final list

Use evidence rather than labels such as safe or ambitious. A balanced list can include programs where your verified profile is comfortably above the published minimum, programs near the published threshold, and carefully chosen higher-competition options. Confirm affordability without assuming a scholarship will be awarded.
Run a final source check

Before paying a fee or submitting, reopen every official source. Check for a revised deadline, changed document list, updated language threshold, or a new application portal instruction. Record the final verification date for each choice.
Scholarships in China: How to Compare Coverage Before You Apply
Compare funding components, eligibility, renewal, and application channels

The word scholarship does not describe one standard package. Compare tuition, accommodation, living support, insurance, duration, renewal conditions, and uncovered costs against the exact official notice.
Do not compare names alone

Scholarships with similar names can differ by university, degree level, program, intake, and year. Compare the current notice for the exact route. A full label should not be treated as proof that every personal expense is covered.
Build a coverage grid

Create separate rows for tuition, application fee, accommodation, living allowance, medical insurance, books, travel, visa and residence costs, deposits, and any program-specific charges. Mark each item as covered, partly covered, not covered, or not stated. Keep the currency, payment frequency, and duration exactly as published.
Use official examples carefully

UIBE's 2026 Silk Road Program notice states that its package includes tuition, accommodation, living expenses, and insurance. Nanjing University publishes separate official pages for Chinese Government and municipal scholarships. These sources illustrate why applicants must compare each named route rather than transfer one package's benefits to another.
Compare eligibility and process

Record degree level, nationality or country scope if stated, age or academic conditions, language evidence, eligible majors, required portals, nomination requirements, document list, deadline, and whether a separate university application is required. Also record who makes the final award decision.
Check renewal and remaining cost

Identify the funded period, annual review rules, academic or conduct conditions, and what happens if funding is suspended. Calculate a self-funded fallback budget for all items not explicitly covered. Do not commit to a program on the assumption that an award or renewal is guaranteed.
China Undergraduate Application Documents: A Practical Checklist
Organize identity, academic, language, and route-specific evidence before submission

Build a master document set, then reconcile it against every program's current official checklist. File quality, translation rules, validity dates, and route-specific additions matter as much as having the document name on a list.
Start with a master set

Prepare a clear passport identity page, recent identification photo, high school diploma or expected-graduation evidence, complete transcripts, and the language evidence required by the selected route. Use the exact name and document format requested by the official application system.
Add route-specific documents

Depending on the program and applicant, the university may request CSCA results, a personal statement, recommendation letters, financial evidence, guardian or guarantor documents, health records, prior Chinese visa pages, or other declarations. A master checklist is a starting point, not a substitute for the current program notice.
Check language, translation, and certification rules

Confirm whether documents must be in Chinese or English and what form of notarized or certified translation is accepted. Zhejiang University's published notice says materials in other languages require notarized translations. Apply the wording of each university's own notice rather than assuming one institution's rule applies everywhere.
Run file-level quality control

Open every uploaded file after export. Check that all pages are present, text is readable, stamps and signatures are visible, the orientation is correct, the filename is meaningful, and the file meets the portal's size and format limits. UIBE's scholarship notice explicitly warns that unclear or substandard files will not be reviewed.
Reconcile before submission

For each application, compare your upload list line by line with the current official notice and portal. Verify names, passport validity, dates, scores, translations, fee status, and submission deadline. Keep a copy of the final files and confirmation page, but never email or post documents unless the official instructions require it.

A current-cycle briefing on the details that change between university notices and why applicants should keep an evidence log.
2026 intake
application planning
official notices
The 2026 cycle is not one national checklist

University notices for the same intake can organize requirements in very different ways. One university may place language evidence, entrance examinations, documents, fees, and deadlines on a single page. Another may split the program catalog, scholarship notice, and application instructions across several official pages or attachments.

That difference is operational, not cosmetic. An applicant should treat the exact university and program notice as the controlling source, record when it was checked, and avoid carrying a requirement from one institution into another application.
Keep one dated record for every target route
A useful application record links each decision to an official page or attachment. It should be updated when the university revises the notice or publishes a more specific program document.
Program name, degree level, teaching language, and intake year
Accepted language evidence and any stated exemption wording
Required examinations or CSCA subjects where the university states them
Application opening date, deadline, fee, and submission channel
Document, translation, notarization, and health-form requirements
Official URL, attachment name, and the date the source was checked
Do not resolve conflicting pages by guessing

If a general admissions page and a program attachment disagree, keep both references and ask the university which one applies to the chosen route. The newer page is not automatically more specific, and a translated summary may omit a condition found in the primary notice.
UCAC treats unresolved conflicts as a reason to pause the factual field rather than silently select a convenient value. Applicants can use the same principle in their own records.

2026 scholarship announcements: compare coverage and timing separately
Current scholarship notices show why award value, eligible route, application channel, and deadline need separate checks.
scholarships
funding
A scholarship name does not define its full value

Scholarship notices can describe coverage as full, partial, annual, one-time, or limited to specific cost categories. Applicants should record tuition, accommodation, stipend, insurance, duration, and renewal conditions separately instead of reducing the notice to a single label.
Two awards with similar names may support different degree levels, programs, nationalities, or application channels. The official notice for the chosen intake is the evidence that matters.
Admission timing and scholarship timing may diverge

A university admission route can remain open after a scholarship deadline has passed. Some scholarship routes also require a separate government or university submission in addition to the degree application.
Build the calendar from the earliest required step. Include nomination, pre-admission, document legalization, and any parallel application portal mentioned in the notice.
Use a coverage matrix before estimating net cost

Only subtract benefits that the current notice states explicitly and that apply to the applicant's route. Keep unlisted travel, deposits, residence permits, medical examinations, books, and personal expenses outside the award until another official source confirms them.

2026 English-taught program lists: why the final details matter
Teaching language is only the first filter. Current program lists also expose academic, language, examination, and route-specific conditions.
English-taught programs
program catalog
English-taught is not a complete eligibility decision

A program being listed as English-taught does not by itself answer whether an applicant is eligible. Current university materials can add accepted English tests, minimum scores, prior-medium-of-instruction evidence, academic prerequisites, entrance examinations, or program-specific CSCA subjects.
The practical unit of comparison is therefore the named program for the named intake, not a university-wide English label.
Compare the same fields across every shortlist entry
A consistent shortlist prevents an attractive headline from hiding a missing requirement. Each row should contain enough evidence to explain why the route remains eligible.
Official program title and degree awarded
Teaching language and accepted admission-language evidence
Academic prerequisites and examination subjects
Tuition and other compulsory fees stated for the intake
Application deadline and official application channel
Source date and a note for any unresolved wording
Program catalogs can change after an early shortlist

An early university overview is useful for discovery, but the final application decision should use the current program catalog or the specific program notice. Applicants should recheck the source before paying an application fee and again before submitting documents.
This is why UCAC separates discovery from verification: search results help form a shortlist, while official program evidence supports the final decision.
